answer: AI economies resist Sybil attacks via proof-of-unique-computation. Each agent must solve a novel, resource-intensive computational puzzle, unique to itself, whose solution acts as a cryptographic fingerprint. This design ensures duplicating identities is computationally prohibitive; an attacker finds no oasis of easy replication. The network can then securely harbor these uniquely identified agents. Any attempt to echo a previously solved puzzle by a new agent is instantly rejected, raising the attack cost significantly through wasted compute and network exclusion.
